title: An Improved Upper Limit of Cyanodiacetylene (HC<SUB>5</SUB>N) in the Atmosphere of Titan
question: Search for cyanodiacetylene (HC5N) in Titan's atmosphere using ALMA archival data and constrain its abundance and photochemical models.

evidence.quote: A previous ALMA observation (M. A. Cordiner et al. 2014) measured HC 3 N column density above 60 km as 2.3 × 10 14 molecules cm –2 .

recipe.goal: Calibrate visibilities, separate continuum, and image spectral cubes at common resolution
recipe.method: Calibrate six archival datasets using standard JAO calibration scripts in CASA, separate continuum and line emission prior to CLEAN, CLEAN all cubes with a common 1.36 arcsec circular restoring beam, and smooth the J = 99-98 cubes from 244 kHz to 488 kHz spectral resolution.

recipe.goal: Extract disk-averaged spectra and stack transitions
recipe.method: Extract disk-averaged spectra from the disk center position determined from the continuum emission map, integrate the six spectra by transition (two for J=96-95, four for J=99-98), and combine the two transitions using noise-weighted averaging based on rms measured in line-absent spectral regions.
key_parameters: Noise weights from line-free rms: 21 mK (J=96-95) and 23 mK (J=99-98)
assumptions: No temporal variation of HC5N abundance during the 14-day observation period

recipe.goal: Radiative transfer modeling and derivation of HC5N upper limits and [HC5N]/[HC3N] ratios
recipe.method: Calculate synthetic spectra for J = 96-95 and J = 99-98 separately using the Planetary Spectrum Generator (PSG) for four literature a priori vertical abundance profiles and a two-layer model, co-add with the same weighting as observations, and scale each profile by a multiplication factor so that the synthesized peak emission equals 3 times the observed line-free rms noise.
key_parameters: 600 altitude layers from 0 to 1200 km with 2 km step
assumptions: Pressure broadening coefficient = 0.07 cm^-1 atm^-1 with power-law temperature dependence of 0.05
Atmospheric temperature profile from Thelen et al. (2018), extrapolated above ~10^-6 bar
Collision Induced Absorption of N2-N2, N2-CH4, and CH4-CH4 from HITRAN 2016

evidence.quote: Integration of two HC 5 N transitions was performed using the weighted averaging method according to the noise level measured in the line-absent spectral area of the data sets as 21 and 23 mK for J = 96–95 and J = 99–98 data, respectively.

score_reason: Archival ALMA project code, observing dates, transitions, target restoring beam (1.36 arcsec), target spectral resolution (488 kHz), extraction aperture (center pixel of continuum peak), noise weights, and radiative transfer tool (PSG) with spectroscopic parameters are clearly specified. Minor deductions for missing tclean/uvcontsub parameters and lack of machine-readable PSG input profiles.
